title: Barbell Back Squat | Exercise Demo
description:
In this video, Red Dot Fitness shows you the Barbell Back Squat.

Red Dot Fitness: https://www.reddotfitness.net/

Coaching Cues:

Body Position: Feet shoulder width apart; keep eyes forward.

Grip: Hands grip the bar hard, evenly spaced on either side of your body, maintaining constant tension by pulling hands apart & bar into your back.

Movement: Initiate by pushing hips back slightly and bend at the knees. Ideally, knees should flex to a 90 degree angle minimum.
Keep torso upright, neutral spine, and feet flat on the ground. Push through heels/midfoot to upright position, and repeat.

Stability: Brace core, keep chest high and shoulder blades pulled back.

description:

✨Seated Leg Curl Machine Tips:✨
-Adjust the back of the seat until the side of your knee lines up with the red pivot point on the machine
-Adjust the range of motion for the movement by moving the leg pad. The closer the leg pad is to the
floor = lesser range of motion
-Adjust the leg pad so it rests between your ankle & calf on the back of your leg

-Maintain good control & avoid using momentum as you flex & extend your knees
-Avoid doing "one rep maxes" on this machine.
Choose a weight that you can do AT LEAST 6 repetitions with

title: How To Do A Barbell Hip Thrust
description:
Once you've mastered the bodyweight hip thrust, adding weight can help to overload the glutes and hamstrings and continue to build strength and size. The barbell is the most popular way to add weight to hip thrusts.

1. Sit with your shoulders and back against the bench.
2. Position the barbell above so it's in line with your hip.
3. Bend the knees with feet firmly planted on the floor. Make sure your feet are at a distance, that allows you to extend your hip whilst keeping your upper back in contact with the bench.
4. Place your hands over the barbell about shoulder width apart. Brace your core and lift your hips up to the ceiling by squeezing your glutes.
5. Pause as you hit the top and then slowly lower back to starting position.

title: The Dumbbell Bench Press: Gym Shorts (How To)
description:
New to the dumbbell bench press or looking for a quick technique tutorial?  Learn correct form in one short video.  

The dumbbell bench press is an accessory lift that mimics the barbell bench press, but the use of the dumbbells limit the weight and accessibility for many lifters while allowing for each arm to move independently and greater rotation at the shoulder during the execution of the movement. 



This movement requires a bench and two (ideally) equally heavy objects that can easily be grasped, such as dumbbells, kettlebells, or adjustable dumbbells. 

During the concentric portion of the movement, we internally rotate the shoulders, pronate the forearms, and twist the dumbbell to be roughly perpendicular with the bench. During the eccentric portion of the movement, we externally rotate the shoulders, supinate the forearms, and twist the dumbbell to be closer to parallel with the bench (roughly 45 degrees).

We tend to program these for advanced athletes who both have access to dumbbells and want to build muscle to enable greater strength for the muscles that contribute to the barbell bench press (or--maybe--who simply want to get more jacked).

Because it's hard to perform these at high intensities, we recommend programming higher rep sets: 2-5 x 6-15. 

These are generally performed near the end of the workout, after the bigger barbell movements have been performed, and they can be performed in a circuit or in a superset with other exercises. 

If you're advanced athlete looking to build your bench press (or the muscle that contribute to the bench press) consider adding the dumbbell bench press to your program.

Gym Shorts videos provide short video demonstrations of correct form for various exercises.

Follow these steps:
-Rest dumbbells on thighs
-Lie back: keep your arms flexed and the dumbbells close to your torso
-Dumbbells begin at ~45 degrees to bench
-Hands roughly in line with sternum
-Dumbbells end ~90 degrees to bench and directly over shoulders
-Elbows fully extended at the top
-Internal rotation on the way up
-External rotation on the way down
-Feet flat on the floor 
-Legs angled out
-Move dumbbells to thighs as you sit up

title: Dumbbell Chest Fly: Demonstration
description:
Instructions:
1. Lie on a bench, and lift a pair of dumbbells up to the starting position.
2. With almost completely straight arms, lower the dumbbells with control out to your sides.
3. When you’ve lowered the dumbbells as deep as possible, reverse the motion and return the dumbbells to the starting position.
4. Repeat for reps.

Commentary:
The dumbbell chest fly is an isolation exercise for your chest muscles and front deltoids. Because the moment arm of the resistance is long when you are in the heaviest portion of the lift, it is easy to accidentally choose too heavy weights for this exercise, with sacrifices in technique as a consequence.

The resistance curve is quite uneven in chest flyes, as the working muscles are almost completely unloaded in the top position. An alternative execution of the exercise could be to avoid the top portion of the movement, and instead reverse the motion just before you reach it, to keep tension in the working muscles. An alternative exercise to avoid this issue would be cable chest flyes or machine chest flyes, where the resistance curve is more even.

Primary Muscles Worked:
- Chest

Secondary Muscles Worked:
- Front Deltoid

title: How To Do Dumbbell Shoulder Press | Exercise Demo
description:
The dumbbell shoulder press is a fantastic exercise for the shoulder muscles! This classic deltoid exercise is perfect for building stronger shoulders!

This exercise targets your shoulders, whilst also engaging your pectoralis major, triceps and serratus anterior.

Starting Position:
- Begin this exercise by sitting with your back against an upright bench
- Take hold of a pair of dumbbells 
- Dumbbells held at shoulder height with a pronated grip

Execution:
- Press the dumbbells overhead, bringing the dumbbells close together at the top of the movement
- Slowly lower the weight back to shoulder level and repeat!

One of the key benefits to the seated dumbbell shoulder press (aka dumbbell overhead press) is that this exercise allows your shoulder muscles to grow evenly. Unlike the barbell shoulder press, where you're able to rely on one shoulder over the other to help you lift the weight.

Developing your shoulder muscles through this exercise can also improve your bench pressing performance!

title: Onnit Tutorials | Dumbbell Lateral Raise Exercise
description:
If you want to know how to incorporate the dumbbell lateral raise into your workout check out the following article for more information: 

https://www.onnit.com/academy/the-best-shoulder-exercises-and-workouts-for-women

You know these already. There may be no better exercise for hitting the lateral head of the deltoid—the middle part that really gives your shoulders some width when looking at them from the front. If you feel a little pinch in your shoulders doing these, try bending your hips a bit so your torso leans forward. This should alleviate some pressure on the joints. Another tip: don’t squeeze the dumbbell handles too hard. Think of your hands as merely hooks to hold the weight. That way, your deltoids will take on more of the load (it won’t be dispersed to your hands and forearms).

Dumbbell lateral raises are tried and true, but you can also perform the lateral raise motion one arm at a time using a barbell in a landmine unit. In this instance, you lift the bar as if it were a long lever, which offers a number of benefits. For one thing, the movement becomes more strict—you can’t really get sloppy and swing the weight up like you might have a tendency to do with dumbbells. For another, you get to work the deltoids in three planes of motion in the same exercise. Most shoulder moves have you lifting weights either out to the sides or overhead, but a landmine lateral raise has a bar path that goes forward and rotates to the side—so it works all the deltoid musculature while still isolating the stress of the exercise to the shoulder. For more on this movement, see The Best Full-Gym Shoulder Workout For Women below.

description:
In this video, Red Dot Fitness shows you the Face Pull with Cables.

Coaching Cues:

Set up: Set band or cable to about eye-level height.

Body Position: Stand facing attachment. Feet shoulder width. Arms reach straight out to grip band or cable rope attachment. Tension in cable/band at start. 

Grip: Pronated - overhand.

Stability: Brace core and squeeze glutes. Keep chest up and maintain vertical torso.

title: How To Do Forearm Plank | Exercise Demo
AB EXERCISE - How to do an abdominal crunch (ab crunch)
description:
Often confused with sit ups, ab crunches challenge the performer to lift their upper back and shoulders off the floor, strengthening the rectus abdominis. 
Unlike sit ups where the entire torso is raised, the lower back stays glued to the floor with ab crunches. While this means it uses less muscles than the sit up, it’s still a valid exercise and can be helpful for beginners with little core strength who struggle to protect the lower back in a sit up. 

How To Do Ab Crunches:
1) Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent so that your feet can remain flat on the floor.
2) Cross your arms over your chest so that each hand is touching the opposing shoulder. Alternatively, rest your hands on your thighs.
3) Begin the reps by flexing your spine to lift your shoulders and upper back off the floor. Think about squeezing your abs and curling your sternum towards your belly button. Your lower back should remain in contact with the floor throughout. 
4) Take a short pause at the top of the movement before slowly lowering yourself to revert to the starting position.

title: 🚶‍♀️Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to do brisk walking:Brisk Walking Technique 🚶‍♀️
description:
Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to do brisk walking:

Brisk Walking Technique 🚶‍♀️

1. Start with a warm-up: Walk at a normal pace for 5-10 minutes.
2. Increase your pace: Gradually increase your walking speed to a brisk pace.
3. Maintain good postureKeep your head up, shoulders relaxed, and engage your core.
4. Take longer strides Try to take slightly longer strides than your normal walking pace.
5. Quick turnover Aim for a quick turnover of your feet, with your feet striking the ground midfoot or forefoot.
6. *Keep your arms relaxed*: Keep your arms relaxed and bent at around a 90-degree angle.
7. *Swing your arms*: Swing your arms forward and backward as you walk.

Cool Down 🔄

1. *Gradually slow down*: Gradually slow down your walking pace to a normal pace.
2. *Stretch*: Stretch your major muscle groups, including your legs, hips, and back.

title: Close Grip Wall Push-up Young Adult Male
description:
Stand approximately arm's length away from a wall, facing the wall.  Place your hands against the wall and position your feet shoulder width apart.
Place your hands slightly closer than shoulder width apart and slightly below your shoulders.  Your thumbs should almost be touching each other.
Position your feet far enough from the wall that your body is at a slight angle to the wall.  Keep your head straight throughout the movement.
Keeping your elbows close to your torso, bend your arms and lower your body toward the wall.  Stop when your chest is 1 to 2 inches away from the wall.
Hold the position for 1 to 2 seconds and contract your chest and arms, pushing your body upward.  Do not lock your elbows at the top of the movement.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
